questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was searching for something rather similar to Denmark and danish culture, but still wished to try something different - The Netherlands was the perfect mixture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not really offered, but I showed up at the front desk at the university one day and there they helped me figure out the discrepancies I expierenced in my schedule

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Again, there was quite a bit of confusion on which courses I had been admitted to and which I had not. I got the help I needed two days prior to the first lecture, but had tried all summer and even before - quite frustrating

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: quite difficult, I succeeded through Facebook groups

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Leiden has no on campus housing, but I would much recommend for future exchange students to get housing through duwo or similar dormitories - even though I could not get a room before hand, I had friends living there and multiple rooms where available - sometimes its better to just rent something the first couple of weeks of being at the host destination and then figure out the housing situation, even though I know how stressfull I would find that myself - you win in regards to social interactions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: finding courses and applying to them was not too difficult, but Leiden do not offer that many anthropology courses - and many of them would be too similar to the ones I have already taken in Copenhagen, why it was difficult to find enough ects within my own faculty - I ended up doing a double major in dutch standards, and even though the courses where very interesting I would not recommend that to anyone - the burden was at times too much

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator was very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very  - I ended up taking which ever courses was advised, as it got too close the start of the semester

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply early, but don't expect to get the courses you think at first

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level was quite similar to that of Copenhagen, but the study load why more extensive. I found it rather challenging ro balance school and social life due to this, but am also really appreciative of the challenge

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much more classroom oriented - rather different

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to international organisations (IO)
Religion in the world
Economy and Ecology
Digital Anthropology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
IO is too intensive as it takes place over only one block and is a very fundamental course for that education - it is however rather fun to take a class in the hauge, so I would recommend that.

Economy and ecology was my favourite course - super interesting

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Don't park your bike illegaly - the municipality will take it and you'll have to pay to get it back

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is expensive, but groceries 20-30% cheaper than in Denmark. I did not have to buy books for school

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was some, but exchange students where not really a part of it

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different clubs for the different faculties - also something called ESN, which I know people thought was fund to participate in different activities through, such as trips to other dutch cities or parties

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: just say yes to everything

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to other cities - Leiden is so central! you can get to Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Harlem, Antwerp, Brussels and much more in a very short time

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I really liked living in the Netherlands and Leiden is a beautiful town, but it is rather small - I don't think I was expecting to live in such a small place, so that was something I had to learn - I spend a lot of my times with friends in Amsterdam, so I got the best of both worlds

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I spoke to almost no dutch people. Leiden is very much an international school and I found that there is quite a divide between the internationals and the dutch, unfortunately - I would say the best way to get in contact with dutch people is on social media :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any big cultural differences, but rather surprising to find it such an international university. Also that they have both midterms and finals - a lot of exams!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the cities and their architecture - dinning out culture is also great! especially in Amsterdam - a lot of places turn in to parties during the night, which is always fun

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try and get a room through Duwo
2. Don't forget to take care of yourself and your social life during exam seasons 
3. Explore Amsterdam and other cities - Leiden is cute but small

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don't feel like you have all the information or answers before arrival, go to the student help desk - it helped me a lot

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting new people and learning to study in a different way

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the same as the most rewarding parts - but that's great I guess

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: overall I find that the help available from UCPH coordinators pre-departure to have been lacking. I would strongly encourage more meetings or office hours - not only for those outside of europe. We felt quite lost.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
